title: The Late Interior
premise: Silas Thornbury, once a celebrated piano prodigy who vanished from the conservatory at nineteen, has spent twenty years invisible as its night janitor. When his childhood home — the house where his mother, Vera, a legendary teacher, raised her students alongside her children — goes up for auction, Silas is forced back among siblings and former pupils who each remember a different woman. As Vera's dementia deepens, the family races to settle the estate and the question beneath it: what really happened the night Silas stopped playing. The truth — that Vera sacrificed Silas's career to protect his brother's secret — finally surfaces, and Silas chooses loyalty to memory over the comfortable lie, playing one last time in the empty sold house before handing over the keys.
about_author: Lior Sterling is the pen name of a writer who spent a decade working nights in institutional buildings while writing before dawn. Their fiction explores the quiet violence of families that organize themselves around a single unspoken fact.

chapters.title: The Smile That Ends Conversations
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. We meet him mopping the conservatory's practice halls at 3 a.m., dodging a young faculty member who recognizes his name from old recordings. The chapter establishes his perfected invisibility and ends with a letter: the Thornbury house enters auction in six weeks. Emotional beat: dread disguised as indifference.

chapters.title: Inventory of a House
chapters.summary: Silas returns to the house for the estate appraisal, cataloguing objects with his sister Margot, who has appointed herself executor. Every room triggers competing memories; they argue over a photograph of four children at the piano. POV alternates between Silas and Margot. Emotional beat: grief sharpening into territorial resentment.

chapters.title: Vera, In Fragments
chapters.summary: Silas visits their mother at Fernwood Care, where Vera drifts between decades, sometimes calling him by his brother Daniel's name. She hums a piece Silas never performed publicly — one he composed at fifteen. His POV. Emotional beat: tenderness laced with fear that she'll remember too much or not enough.

chapters.title: The Auction Catalogue
chapters.summary: The auctioneer wants provenance stories for the sale catalogue; former students begin arriving with their own Vera legends, each flattering and slightly false. Daniel arrives from abroad, charming, evasive. Silas's POV with an interlude of a student's letter from 1998. Emotional beat: the past being curated into something saleable.

chapters.title: What Margot Kept
chapters.summary: Margot's POV. Sorting the attic, she finds a sealed envelope in Vera's handwriting marked 'For after' — and hides it rather than share it. Flashbacks reveal Margot's lifelong role as the family's keeper of appearances. Emotional beat: guilt curdling into justification.

chapters.title: The Night It Stopped
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, moving between present and the winter he was nineteen: a competition, a broken hand that was never explained, a withdrawal no one questioned. Daniel's behavior that season surfaces in half-memories. The brothers have a strained dinner where Daniel nearly says something and doesn't. Emotional beat: rising pressure under civility.

chapters.title: Bidding War
chapters.summary: A developer outbids the family's modest pooled offer; the auction becomes public spectacle, drawing press to the 'home of a legend.' Vera, briefly lucid during a visit, tells Silas the house was never hers to sell. Silas's POV. Emotional beat: panic — time is running out on both the house and her memory.

chapters.title: For After
chapters.summary: Margot, unable to carry it alone, gives Silas the envelope: Vera's written account of the night Silas's hand was injured — Daniel caused it, drunk and jealous, and Vera buried it to save them both, sacrificing Silas's career as the price of silence. Silas's POV. Emotional beat: devastation and terrible clarity.

chapters.title: The Question the Family Arranged Itself Around
chapters.summary: Climax. Silas confronts Daniel and Margot in the emptied house days before closing. Daniel confesses; Margot admits she knew and chose the family's peace over Silas's life. Silas must decide whether exposing the truth serves anyone now that Vera can't be held accountable. He chooses truth within the family, not the press. Emotional beat: rupture and release.

chapters.title: Last Light in the Front Room
chapters.summary: Resolution. On the final day, Silas brings Vera to the vacant house; she mistakes it for a lesson day and asks him to play. He sits at the bare floor where the piano stood and plays his own unfinished piece from age fifteen, completing it for the first time. They leave together; he keeps the smile, but now it opens conversations. Emotional beat: belonging redefined — carried, not housed.
